extracted.intended_audience: science communicators, university/public-research PR officers, science journalists, and scholars of science communication
extracted.subtask_description: Producing and evaluating university or research-institute press releases as a form of science communication, with attention to framing, professionalization, media uptake, and the relationship to independent science journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing and owning stories about science
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific institutions have for a long time known the importance of framing and owning stories about science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate press releases on how they frame scientific findings and whether the institution is positioning itself to 'own' the narrative; consider how framing shapes public understanding and agenda-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release as an effective way of communicating science
rubrics_metrics.description: They also know the effective way of communicating science in a press release. This is part of the institution’s public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the press release as a communication tool designed for media uptake and institutional messaging; assess clarity, salience, and PR-oriented goals (rather than purely scholarly exposition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalization and communicative competences inside institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhanced competition among research institutions has led to a buildup of communicative competences and professionalization of public relations inside the institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the level of professional PR practice behind a release (training, strategic messaging, media relations) as a factor affecting content quality, reach, and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of press releases into institutional science communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The press release has become an integrated part of science communication from these institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether press releases are central to an institution's outward science communication strategy and how that integration influences what is communicated and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media working conditions and re-use of press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Changing working conditions in the media, where fewer people have to publish more, have made press releases from trustworthy scientific institutions into free and easily copied content for the editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate press releases with awareness of newsroom constraints: measure how likely content is to be republished verbatim, and whether releases are written to be 'copy-ready' for overburdened editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthiness of the issuing institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases from trustworthy scientific institutions [are] free and easily copied content for the editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional reputation/trustworthiness as a criterion for media pickup and public acceptance; the same wording from a less trusted source may be treated differently by journalists and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing public relations from science communication
rubrics_metrics.description: This is part of the institution’s public relations. (Context: public communication from research institutes: is it science communication or public relations?)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating releases, probe whether the primary aim is PR (image/visibility) or genuine public-interest science communication (accuracy, context, critical nuance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the critical and independent science journalist
rubrics_metrics.description: I especially take a close look at the role of the critical and independent science journalist in relation to this corporate controlled communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess press releases in relation to journalistic scrutiny: good practices include enabling independent verification, providing context, and not precluding critical reporting; judge how releases either facilitate or hinder independent critique.
